assumptions.obligation: i_full_thr is static. It is written once before use and stays stable (on the global clock) from the first time both hardware resets are released until the end of the trace.
i_empty_thr is static. It is written once before use and stays stable (on the global clock) from the first time both hardware resets are released until the end of the trace.
No write (i_wr_en=0) while either hardware reset is asserted.
No read (i_rd_en=0) while either hardware reset is asserted.
i_rst_n_wr is released only at a rising edge of i_clk_wr (synchronized release, low for at least one write edge). Assertion is asynchronous and free.
i_rst_n_rd is released only at a rising edge of i_clk_rd (synchronized release, low for at least one read edge). Assertion is asynchronous and free.
After a hardware reset of only one domain, no write until both domains have been reset with overlapping reset windows and both are released. Assertion and release times can differ.
After a hardware reset of only one domain, no read until both domains have been reset with overlapping reset windows and both are released. Assertion and release times can differ.

notes:
I made two changes, and they cover all four counterexamples. I have not re-run the formal check, so whether they now pass is unconfirmed.

(1) Reset pairing (ENV-07/08, CHK-002, CHK-003, CHK-013). Traffic is now allowed only after the two hardware resets overlap: both are low at the same time at some point in the window, then both are released. Before, a reset of the read domain followed later by a separate reset of the write domain counted as 'both domains reset'. That let a stale synchronized pointer from the first domain stay in the second domain's synchronizer after the window closed. Basis in the spec: AF-12-07 and AF-7.2-12 say a reset of only one domain leaves an inconsistent state that the IP neither detects nor repairs. AF-10.7.4-24 says that on a hardware reset both FSMs, both pointers and all synchronizers go to their reset values 'at once'. 'Need not be asserted together' (AF-3-36, AF-7.2-11) is still respected: the two resets can be asserted and released at different times. They only have to overlap. After a reset of one domain alone, traffic stays blocked until a reset of both domains with overlap. This only removes behaviour that the spec calls undefined.

(2) Static thresholds (ENV-01/02, CHK-004, CHK-013). The spec says 'written once before use' (AF-6.2-10, AF-7.2-04, AF-20.2-07). It also gives the thresholds a false path (AF-17.1.3-04), so they are asynchronous to both clocks. The thresholds are therefore now checked on the global clock: they must stay stable from the first time both resets are released until the end of the trace. Before, the check was only clock-sampled and only while both resets were high. That allowed a change while one domain was still using the FIFO. This is stronger than 'stable while in use', but it is what the spec text and the designer decision cited by triage say. If the designer wants to allow changing the thresholds while both domains are in reset, relax the condition to allow changes only when both resets are low.

No assumption was added on i_rst_n_sw, i_wr_data, or on accesses while full, empty or blocked. Those stay free because the spec calls them legal.
